To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) clinicians in community mental health agencies do not routinely assess key clinical domains in older persons; (2) clinicians in community agencies do not routinely plan services that address the needs of older persons and their caregivers; (3) a guided assessment and planning intervention can significantly improve clinicians' practices; and (4) the intervention was associated, at least in the short term, with improved outcomes for older adults.
the guided assessment and service plan-ning intervention was associated with significant improvement in the clinical practices of community mental health clinicians caring for older adults.
the intervention improved the specificity of treatment plans and the quality and comprehensiveness of assessments of older adults.

the development and evaluation of interventions to improve the quality and effectiveness of mental health services for older persons.
developing and evaluating a model of community mental health services that can be used to improve the mental health outcomes of older adults.
the development of a new, comprehensive and integrated model of care for older adults with mental health problems.

this study provides the first evidence that a brief, guided assessment and service plan intervention can improve the clinical practices of community mental health providers in caring for older adults.
